card: This pull request makes common::WriteSettings write to a temporary file and atomically replace the target destination with RenameOver. Previously, banlist.json was written directly in place, leaving node operators vulnerable to a truncated or corrupted banlist if the write was interrupted by a crash or power failure. It also removes duplicate temporary-file management logic in ArgsManager::WriteSettingsFile and adds unit tests covering atomic banlist writes and rename failure handling.
evidence: PR description: "WriteJson writes to path + ".tmp" and RenameOver()s into place, so a failed or interrupted write cannot leave a truncated destination. Both settings.json and banlist.json use this helper."
problem: Writing banlist.json previously wrote directly to the destination path. A crash, power loss, or write failure while persisting bans could leave the file empty or truncated. Additionally, ArgsManager had to implement its own atomic-write dance around settings.json rather than having the utility function handle it.
scope_notes: The PR description mentions renaming common::WriteSettings to common::WriteJson, but the patch leaves the function name as WriteSettings.
summary: Moves atomic file replacement logic directly into common::WriteSettings by writing to a temporary ".tmp" file and using RenameOver to replace the target destination. This makes banlist writes atomic and removes duplicate temporary-file handling from ArgsManager::WriteSettingsFile. A unit test is added to verify banlist roundtripping and rename-failure behavior.
